root cause: `npabridge/payload.py` emitted the dladdr result check as `cbnz w0, publish_old`, but dladdr reports success with a non-zero result, so a successful lookup was treated as a failure; the basename scan also stopped at the first '/', so an absolute dli_fname could never match its basename. Both were present since the first payload commit b146213, so the dispatch had never activated

fix: test the dladdr result with CBZ and compare the final path component (the scan reaches the NUL, then steps back over the basename and requires the preceding byte to be '/'). `npabridge.payload` now asserts both shapes on every assembly

root cause: the app's FFmpeg 4.4 still numbers three AVPixelFormat members that 9.0.2 removed (AV_PIX_FMT_VAAPI_MOCO, AV_PIX_FMT_VAAPI_IDCT, AV_PIX_FMT_XVMC) and they sit inside the enum, so every value from legacy 46 on is shifted (+2 up to 153, +3 after). two defects were found and fixed during the earlier part of this pass, both in the shim: (1) the shadow codecpar->extradata aliased the modern buffer, so the app's av_freep of attachment extradata double-freed at the modern close (SIGABRT in codec_parameters_reset); the shadow now owns a copy. (2) libavcodec/libavutil renumber AVCodecID and AVPixelFormat across major versions, so the copied values mis-resolved (HEVC 172 vs 173, VP9 166 vs 167, AV1 222 vs 32797, ASS 94230 vs 96269, OTF 98310 vs 100355, YUV420P10LE 62 vs 64). A compiler-generated name-based table (deps/gen_demux_enum_map.py) now translates codec_id and format. This is why HEVC/WebM and the embedded subtitle/fonts failed before. Neither the demux (open/find_stream_info returned 0 and read_frame only reached EOF) nor the app's decode path was at fault

the end-of-branch review then found a third layout drift: AVChapter moved across majors (the modern id is int64_t, so time_base is at 0x8 not 0x4). modern_to_shadow had aliased the modern array, so chapter timings read as garbage. Commit 26884f1 builds a legacy-shaped AVChapter[] and also syncs shadow->modern in av_read_frame and guards a NULL modern stream slot. The artifact above is the one that carries this fix, and the chaptered Matroska row was measured on it

the custom-IO path turned out to be the main path, not a side route: the app always feeds libavformat through its own AVIOContext (avio_alloc_context with a zero-size buffer, then ctx->pb), so the ordinary playback rows already covered the FFmpegDemuxer custom-IO open (sub_100AED374) and the thumbnail/metadata row covered the MediaInfoFetcher probe (sub_100A3E1F8) - see notes/ida-investigation-demux-custom-io.md. this acceptance round found and fixed four defects, in one commit (ae47874): (1) npa_ctx_out never published ctx->codec (0x10), which the app tests at 0x100A04D00 and bails out of decoding when it is NULL - so find_decoder/open2 succeeded and decode_subtitle2 was never called; (2) it never published ctx->extradata (0x58/0x60), which the app's ASS setup reads at 0x100A047F8 to seed libass, so the script header arrived empty; (3) npa_subdec_avsubtitle_free read entry->modern after npa_sub_remove had already released the entry, a use-after-free that aborted in av_free on the first decoded subtitle (crash report frame LibFFmpegCore902Bridge+0x616C, back through sub_100A04BB8 and the delivery loop); (4) the packet copy set pts/dts/duration before av_new_packet, which resets them, so the decoder saw AV_NOPTS_VALUE and duration 0. The decode entry also had to refresh the modern context, because the app writes pkt_timebase after open2 (0x100A03DF4) and only npa_ctx_of was syncing

the behavioural gap that made ASS render nothing: 4.4.x's avcodec_decode_subtitle2 rewrote a Matroska-form ASS event into a standalone `Dialogue: 0,<start>,<end>,...` line (FF_API_ASS_TIMING, gated on sub_text_format, using the packet's pts/duration over pkt_timebase), and 9.0.2 removed both the rewrite and the field. The app forwards rect->ass to libass verbatim (rect->ass at 0x100A05284, strlen at 0x100A0528C, ass_process_data at 0x100A0529C), so on 9.0.2 libass received `0,0,Default,,0,0,0,,CUE-A` and produced no events. The shim now reproduces the 4.4.x rewrite and defaults sub_text_format the way 4.4.x did, because the app allocates its context through the shim and never sees 4.4.x's AVOption default. Evidence: with the fix, libass receives `Dialogue: 0,0:00:00.50,0:00:02.00,Default,,0,0,0,,CUE-A` (x4, timings correct) and render_frame returns a non-NULL image 109 times out of 205, against 110 for the whole-dylib fallback to the app's own 4.4.5

the face: playback and probe/poster software decode now run on 9.0.2 libavcodec. The new ffmpeg-codec domain redirects 12 APIs over 44 call sites - avcodec_alloc_context3 / free_context / find_decoder / open2 / close / flush_buffers / avcodec_parameters_alloc / parameters_free / parameters_from_context / parameters_to_context / avcodec_send_packet / avcodec_receive_frame - reached from the video decoder (sub_100A80F9C onwards), the audio decoder (sub_100A898xx), the probe/poster still extractor (sub_100A467xx) and the shared source-context helper (sub_100A8A4F8). the site count moved from 39 to 44 during the section 7.2 gate: the temporary source context sub_100A8A4F8 allocates is released by five callers, not three, two of them in the SPDIF path (0x100B300F0, 0x100B63F88). Moving only the callers' frees would have left `alloc on 4.4.5, free in the shim`, so with the user's ruling the whole lifetime (12 APIs / 44 sites) is in this unit. The helper's own parameter chain (parameters_alloc/copy/to_context/free) and av_malloc stay on 4.4.5, which is why the shim's alloc_context3 must hand back a shadow that legacy code can keep filling. avcodec_parameters_copy also stays on 4.4.5: both of its operands are legacy-shaped shadows, which 4.4.5's implementation handles correctly as it stands (spec section 2.5)

the parameter translation turned out to be a full round trip on the video open path - source context -> parameters_from_context -> parameters_to_context -> decoder context - and it was seven fields deep: width, height, sample aspect ratio, the colour fields, field order, video delay, profile/level, block align, frame size and the paddings were being dropped. Fixed for every codec type. AVCodecContext.pix_fmt and AVCodecParameters.format must be translated in both directions (4.4 numbering on the app side, spec section 3.3); AVSampleFormat needs none. AVCodecContext.channel_layout had never been published, so npa_ctx_in erased the mask on every entry while the audio frame consumer reads it (0x100A89CA0)

receive_frame materialises each modern frame into the app's own 4.4 AVFrame over a shim-built legacy AVBuffer/AVBufferRef whose refcount the app's own av_frame_unref drives, so the last reference releases the modern frame (the app refs frames into its wrapper at sub_100A817AC). 9.0.2 renamed AVFrame.pkt_duration to duration and repurposed the frame flag bits (CORRUPT/DISCARD are the only shared ones), so the materialisation translates rather than copies. avcodec_close no longer exists in 9.0.2, so the shim implements it as flush + mark closed and leaves the release to the following free_context

a host probe (temporary, outside the repo) caught two defects before the device round: (1) npa_params_of returned the modern object for a shim-owned params shadow without syncing the shadow first, so what the app (or 4.4.5's avcodec_parameters_copy) wrote into a shim-allocated shadow was ignored - this broke the video open path outright, the context arrived with width/height/format zero; (2) the per-call context refresh in send_packet/receive_frame made 9.0.2's H.264 decoder discard every non-key frame (17 of 424 frames decoded). Bisection pinned it to writing avctx->sample_aspect_ratio back per packet; the data path no longer refreshes the context and the configuration entries (open2, parameters_to_context, flush_buffers, the subtitle decode entry) keep it. Rule and measurement recorded in spec section 2.3

AV1, first failure and its resolution: 9.0.2's native av1 decoder is hardware-only - av1dec.c's get_pixel_format() returns AVERROR(ENOSYS) without avctx->hwaccel and the app never passes a hardware device - so AV1 gave a black thumbnail and playback skipped to the next item (find_decoder(32797) -> ok, open2 -> 0, send_packet -> -78, receive_frame -> always EAGAIN). With the user's ruling the closure was given libdav1d (`--enable-libdav1d` plus `--disable-decoder=av1`, so that find_decoder(AV_CODEC_ID_AV1) resolves to the software decoder with no shim-side selection policy - the decoder table is alphabetical, so `av1` would otherwise win). dav1d pinned at 1.5.4 (a 1.5.0 build was replaced before the acceptance install, same series and meson options). Probe after the change: AV1 250/250 frames

AV1, second failure - the H/W regression the user reported - root cause and fix: the app builds the hardware decoder's CMVideoFormatDescription from the AV1 extradata and hands those bytes to VideoToolbox, so their shape decides whether AV1 can play in hardware at all. 4.4.x's matroska demuxer deliberately publishes only the OBUs (its own comment in matroskadec.c: "For now, propagate only the OBUs, if any. Once libavcodec is updated to handle isobmff style extradata this can be removed", implemented as `extradata_offset = 4`), while 9.0.2's libavcodec is that updated version and hands out the whole AV1CodecConfigurationRecord. Located by dumping the AVFormatContext/AVStream/AVCodecParameters shadows field by field in both states - bridge dylib removed (app's own 4.4.5) against the 9.0.2 units - where the extradata was the only difference: 14 bytes of OBUs against an 18-byte record whose first four bytes are that same sequence header OBU. With the record, VideoToolbox was asked for a 0x0 description and answered -12910, so the player fell back to software (VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported('av01') is 1 on the same machine, so the platform was never the problem). Fix: the demux unit strips the record for AV1, exactly what 4.4.x did, and the codec unit puts a record back when the bytes cross into the modern world, because libdav1d rejects anything not starting with marker+version 0x81 and reads the config OBUs that follow; the record's other header fields are filled from what the legacy side already carries (profile, level, pixel format) and only chroma_sample_position is left at unknown, which is informational - the decoders read the real one from the sequence header. Probe after the fix: AV1 250/250 with the OBU-shaped input, that is, through the new translation
